newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Asset swap swells Cons Mining volumes.
newsitem.headline: Asset swap swells Cons Mining volumes.

text.p: Heavy volumes went through South African mining and finance holding company Consolidated Mining Corp Ltd on Monday after an asset swap deal by stockbroking firm Fleming Martin, dealers said.
"There was an asset swap deal involving a foreign buyer today," said a dealer.
The dealer said the deal involved 64 million shares worth around 51 million rand at 80 cents a share.

"It lookes like they (Cons Mining) are quite well off at these levels and obviously there is a lot of jobbers just jumping in on the back of this corporate finance deal and waiting to see what would happen," one Johannesburg Stock Exchange dealer added.
By about 1117 GMT Cons Mining's stock was down a cent at 66 cents after an earlier high of 80 cents with a total of 65.4 million shares valued at 52.1 million rand exchanging hands.

Consmining bought 4.9 million shares from mining firm JCI Ltd at 46 rand each late last month and added that the acquisition emphasised its strategy to enlarge its asset base through appropriate purchases.
